description:
print to a BAREWORD filehandle whose first argument is a GLOB is a whole-statement DROP: `print FOO * 2, "
";` (FOO unknown, never opened) -- perl reads FOO as the filehandle and `*2` as the glob *main::2 (prints to the unopened handle: nothing, and the program continues); PCL announces `statement dropped ... Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []` and the statement dies at run time, so a following `print "end
"` never runs.  PRE-EXISTING (base 5adcc156 identical).  Found by s513b (#2871): the static-parse review probe p16-constlater (`print PI * 2, "
"; use constant PI => 3;`) printed 6 on main because the constant applied above its `use`; with #2871 the name is unknown there, as in perl, and the statement reaches this gap.  Repro:

  print FOO * 2, "
"; print "end
";        perl: end     PCL: (drop, dies)

Realistic shape: rare (an unknown ALL-CAPS word before `*`).  Fix site: the print filehandle-slot decision in PExpr (an unknown bareword followed by a term-starting `*`); probe the multiplication spelling `print FOO * 2` with a DECLARED sub FOO (must stay multiplication).
subject: `print FOO * 2, ...` (unknown bareword, then a glob) is a whole-statement DROP -- perl prints the glob to filehandle FOO
